scenarioStory.history: Patient was cooking in his kitchen when a grease-filled pan flared up and splashed hot grease onto his right forearm. His spouse ran cool water over the area for a few minutes before EMS arrival. He reports immediate, severe burning pain that has not improved, rated 9 out of 10. Denies loss of consciousness, denies other injuries, denies any facial or airway involvement.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 41-year-old male seated at his kitchen table, guarding a visibly burned right forearm. He is alert, oriented, and in severe distress from pain. → Burn cared for, fentanyl given: Crew completes burn wound care, establishes IV access on unburned skin, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain, applying capnography to monitor for opioid-related hypoventilation. → Pain reassessed, repeat fentanyl given: Pain remains significant on reassessment, so a repeat weight-based fentanyl dose is given per protocol. Pain improves and the patient is transported in a position of comfort with continued monitoring.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Burn to right forearm, severe pain

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 41-year-old male seated at his kitchen table, guarding a visibly burned right forearm. He is alert, oriented, and in severe distress from pain.

scenarioEvents.name: Burn cared for, fentanyl given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes burn wound care, establishes IV access on unburned skin, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain, applying capnography to monitor for opioid-related hypoventilation.
relatedChecklist: Stop the burning: remove jewelry and any non-adherent wet clothing from right forearm
Cover burn with dry, clean dressing; do not apply gels or ointments
Estimate TBSA (~4-5%) via Rule of Nines and document baseline pain score of 9/10
Establish IV access on unburned skin (left forearm), avoiding the burned right forearm
Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
Apply waveform capnography to monitor for early hypoventilation after opioid administration

scenarioEvents.name: Pain reassessed, repeat fentanyl given
scenarioEvents.description: Pain remains significant on reassessment, so a repeat weight-based fentanyl dose is given per protocol. Pain improves and the patient is transported in a position of comfort with continued monitoring.
relatedChecklist: Repeat fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg) 5 minutes after first dose for persistent pain
Reassess pain score and vital signs; transport in position of comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Pain management delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew addresses the burn wound but does not establish IV access or administer fentanyl, leaving the patient's severe pain unmanaged. He becomes increasingly anxious and tachycardic.
relatedChecklist: Recognize unmanaged severe pain (9/10); establish IV access and give fentanyl 90 mcg IV per protocol
